chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who struck a man with a stick, and he did not raise the stick until he died. He said: He shall be handed over to the guardians of the slain, but he shall not be left to derive pleasure from it; rather, he shall be executed upon him with the sword.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: The guardians/heirs of the slain — those with the legal right to demand qisas or accept blood money (diya)
key_terms.يُتَلَذَّذُ: Derive pleasure/enjoyment — the concern here is that a prolonged beating-to-death might become a form of torture for the executioners' satisfaction
key_terms.يُجَازُ عَلَيْهِ بِالسَّيْفِ: Retaliation executed by the sword — swift, dignified execution rather than prolonged suffering

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a person who beats another to death with a stick without stopping?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) issues a legal ruling on the case of someone who beats another to death with a stick without stopping. The ruling establishes that the killer must be handed over to the family of the victim for qisas (retaliation), but crucially, he must not be killed in the same manner (beaten with a stick) lest the executioners derive pleasure from a prolonged death — instead, death must be delivered swiftly with a sword. This reflects the Islamic principle that qisas must be proportionate and humane, not involving torture.
word_analysis: he shall be executed/killed in retaliation
